j.shIn.sh.level=0: The S&H LEVEL slider is at 0, so the sample-and-hold reads nothing. Raise LEVEL.

j.vco1Kbd.lfo@init: The LFO now sets the pitch of VCO 1 (up to 1 octave either way). The keyboard no longer reaches it, so it holds the pitch of its frequency slider plus whatever this cable sends.
j.vco1Kbd.audio@init: Oscillator 1 now sets the pitch of VCO 1 (up to 1 octave either way). The keyboard no longer reaches it, so it holds the pitch of its frequency slider plus whatever this cable sends.
j.vco1Kbd.noise@init: The noise generator now sets the pitch of VCO 1 (up to 1 octave either way). The keyboard no longer reaches it, so it holds the pitch of its frequency slider plus whatever this cable sends.
j.vco1Kbd.fast@init: The fast LFO now sets the pitch of VCO 1 (up to 1 octave either way). The keyboard no longer reaches it, so it holds the pitch of its frequency slider plus whatever this cable sends.
j.vco1Kbd.env@init: The envelope now sets the pitch of VCO 1 (up to 1 octave either way). The keyboard no longer reaches it, so it holds the pitch of its frequency slider plus whatever this cable sends.
j.vco1Kbd.kbd@init: VCO 1 follows the keyboard through the cable, just as it does through the internal wiring, so nothing changes.
j.vco1Kbd.kbd2@init: VCO 1 now plays the upper of the two held notes (UPPER VOICE), while the other oscillators play the lower one. With VOICE MODE on DUO you can play two-note chords and lines.

j.vcfRing.lfo@init: The LFO is a slow control signal, not a sound. Fed into the filter in place of the ring modulator it gives clicks and thumps at most.
j.vcfRing.audio@init: The filter now hears oscillator 1 in place of the ring modulator, at the level set by the slider above. The other filter inputs carry on as before.
